questions.stem: A patient's blood report shows: low thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), high T4, normal blood glucose. Which condition is most consistent with these findings?
questions.explanation: In HYPERthyroidism, the thyroid over-secretes T4 independent of pituitary control; elevated T4 negatively feeds back on the pituitary to SUPPRESS TSH → TSH is LOW. In hypothyroidism it would be the reverse (high TSH, low T4). Normal glucose rules out diabetes; Addison's is an adrenal issue. Clinical-inference item. e.g., Graves' disease.

questions.stem: Consider the following about HUMAN BLOOD. 1. Plasma makes up roughly 55 % of whole blood by volume. 2. AB-positive is the universal plasma donor. 3. Mature RBCs in humans lack a nucleus and most organelles. 4. The globin chains of adult haemoglobin (HbA) are two α and two β chains. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is WRONG — AB-positive is the universal RED-CELL RECIPIENT, not the universal plasma donor. The universal PLASMA donor is AB (plasma contains no anti-A or anti-B antibodies). O-negative is the universal red-cell donor. Statements 1, 3, 4 are correct.

questions.stem: ASSERTION (A): A person bitten by a rabid dog is given HUMAN RABIES IMMUNOGLOBULIN (HRIG) in addition to the rabies vaccine. REASON (R): HRIG provides immediate passive antibodies while the vaccine takes 7-14 days to generate an active immune response.

options.option_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

questions.explanation: Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for category-III rabies exposure uses both: HRIG (passive immunity — ready-made antibodies, acts immediately at the bite site) + rabies vaccine (active immunity — takes 1-2 weeks to develop). Rabies incubation is slow (typically 1-3 months), so this combined strategy works.

questions.explanation: Pellagra — Vitamin B3 (Niacin). Scurvy — Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid). Beri-beri — Vitamin B1 (Thiamine). Rickets — Vitamin D (Calciferol). The paired-concept question forces the student to recall all four simultaneously.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the human KIDNEY is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: Each adult kidney contains roughly one million nephrons.
The Loop of Henle establishes the osmotic gradient in the medulla that enables urine concentration.
Reabsorption of glucose is passive and occurs mainly in the collecting duct.
Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) from the posterior pituitary increases water permeability of the collecting duct.

questions.explanation: Glucose reabsorption is ACTIVE (via SGLT transporters) and happens in the PROXIMAL CONVOLUTED TUBULE, not the collecting duct. Under normal conditions ~100 % of filtered glucose is reabsorbed (hence no glucose in normal urine). The other three are correct.

questions.stem: During strenuous exercise, lactic acid accumulates in skeletal muscle. Which of the following best explains WHY?

options.option_text: Oxygen supply falls short of demand, so pyruvate is reduced to lactate by LDH to regenerate NAD⁺ and sustain glycolysis.
Lactic acid is produced directly in the cytoplasm from stored glycogen without any enzyme involvement.
High carbon-dioxide levels convert pyruvate to lactate.

questions.explanation: Under low-O2 (anaerobic) conditions, the electron-transport chain cannot consume NADH fast enough. Cells convert pyruvate → lactate via lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), regenerating NAD⁺ so glycolysis (and ATP production) can continue. Mechanism-centered question — not just 'what', but WHY.

questions.stem: Consider the following about the HUMAN IMMUNE SYSTEM. 1. Innate immunity is present from birth and provides the first line of defence. 2. B-lymphocytes mediate cellular (cell-mediated) immunity. 3. The thymus is the primary site of T-cell maturation. 4. IgM is the first antibody produced during a primary immune response. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is WRONG — B-lymphocytes mediate HUMORAL (antibody-mediated) immunity; T-lymphocytes mediate cell-mediated immunity. Statements 1, 3, 4 are correct: innate is inborn, thymus matures T-cells, IgM is first in any primary response (appears within days; IgG peaks later and is the most abundant).

questions.stem: A baby is born with jaundice (yellow skin) due to blood-group incompatibility. The mother is Rh-negative and the father is Rh-positive. Which explanation is most likely?

options.option_text: The baby is Rh-negative and the mother's anti-A antibodies attacked the baby's red cells.
The baby is Rh-positive; maternal anti-Rh IgG antibodies crossed the placenta and haemolysed fetal red cells (erythroblastosis fetalis).
The baby has Rh-positive cells that attack the mother's blood during delivery.
Jaundice is caused by vitamin D deficiency in the newborn.

questions.explanation: Classic Rh incompatibility. If a prior sensitising event (earlier pregnancy, transfusion) caused the Rh-negative mother to produce anti-D IgG, these small-enough-to-cross-placenta antibodies attack the current Rh-positive fetus's RBCs → haemolysis → neonatal jaundice (erythroblastosis fetalis / haemolytic disease of the newborn). Prevented modernly by giving anti-D (Rho(D) immune globulin) to Rh-neg mothers at 28 weeks + post-delivery.
